subject: mathematics
question_text: If A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} and f: A→B is a surjection defined by f(x) = x² + x + 1 then find B.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.79 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 90.1. The book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages (unlike its LAQ/SAQ pages): the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Appearance years are the book's, board-split. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find B — what you compute, and what the word surjection gives you.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Compute every image
steps.margin_note: One mark for the five values. A has five elements, so compute all five — no shortcuts.

recall.must_convey: That every element of A is substituted, giving the five values 3, 1, 1, 3, 7.
accept: substitute each element f of minus two is three f of minus one is one f of zero is one f of one is three f of two is seven
put all five values in and get three one one three and seven
compute the image of every element of A
anni five values substitute chesi three one one three seven vasthai
the images are three one one three seven

steps.why: B is built from the images, so the images have to exist before B can be named. Two of them repeat, which is what makes the next step interesting.
common_mistakes: Sign slip on f(−2): (−2)² is 4, not −4.
Computing only the positive elements of A.

steps.label: Write B as a set
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the SET. A surjection means B is exactly the range, and a set never repeats an element.
lines: f is a surjection ⇒ B = f(A)

recall.must_convey: That because f is a surjection B equals the range f(A), and that repeated values are written once: B = {1, 3, 7}.
accept: since f is a surjection B is the range so B is one three seven
onto means the codomain equals the range and repeats are written once
B equals the set one three and seven
surjection kabatti B ye range so one three seven
the set is one three seven without repeats

steps.why: Surjection is the whole reason B is pinned down. Without it B could be any set containing the range.
common_mistakes: Giving B = A, or writing the domain instead of the range.
Never using the word surjection, so B is asserted with no reason.
